These Appeals, Coming On For Admission, This
Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice N S Sanjay Gowda
 Oral Judgment
1.
In respect of an accident which had occurred on 30.04.2017, Paramesh who was riding the motor cycle preferred a claim petition.
2. It was the case of claimant that while he was riding his motor cycle he was hit by another two wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JZ-1876 which was owned by NC: 2024:KHC:45514 Kandan N.
He contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the scooter.
3. Kandan entered appearance and contested the petition.

He stated that his vehicle was never involved in the accident and he had parked his scooter on the left side of the road and had gone to attend nature call and at that time, Paramesh who was riding his motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner suffered a skid and had a fall and sustained injuries.
4. He contended that using the registration of his vehicle which was parked by the side of the road he a false complaint had been filed and documents were do documents as if his vehicle was involved in the accident.
5. The insurer also entered appearance and supported the case of the owner.
The Tribunal, by the Mr. R. Parmesh vs Mr. Kandan.

3 NC: 2024:KHC:45514 impugned order, has come to the conclusion that the two wheeler owned by Kandan was in fact being driven by his minor daughter-Jaishree and, therefore, Kandan was liable to pay the compensation.
In order to come to this conclusion, the Tribunal has placed reliance on the chargesheet that has been filed against Jaishree.
The Tribunal has also proceeded to award a sum of Rs.3,28,000/- to Paramesh after finding that he had suffered 11% disability to the whole body and was earning a sum of Rs.9,000/- per month.
6. As a consequence of this award, Kandan, the owner of the vehicle is in appeal, and Paramesh - the claimant is also in appeal seeking for enhancement.

7. Learned counsel for Kandan, the owner of the two wheeler who has been made liable contended that his vehicle was never involved in the accident and this is clear from the IMV report which indicates that there is no damage to both the vehicles.

He NC: 2024:KHC:45514 contended that since his vehicle was parked by the side of the road, unnecessarily, his vehicle was sought to be impleaded by creating that his daughter was riding the two wheeler.

8. Learned counsel for the claimant, however, contends that the accident did occur as a result of Kandan's daughter's driving which was rash and negligent, and the Tribunal was justified in recording the said finding.
It is, however, submitted that the sums awarded are inadequate and the same are required to be enhanced.
9. Since the occurrence of the accident is in serious dispute, it will have to be first decided as to whether the two wheeler owned by the Kandan was involved in the accident.
As stated above, the police after investigation, had laid a chargesheet against Jaishree holding that she was riding the two wheeler that too without driving licence.
In order to establish that Jaishree was not driving and was not involved in the accident, Kandan has not chosen to examine his daughter Jaishree.

However, a clear suggestion is made to the following effect- "zj   Nrwzg. D Aiz g Ai Dv  Vv. 1 Jzgzgg U z  Awzg JAzg jAi."

sentences.text: This suggestion by itself clearly indicates that Jaishree - the daughter of Kandan was present at the spot of the accident.
If this suggestion is accepted, it follows that Jaishree was involved in the accident.
The police after investigation have, in fact, laid a chargesheet holding that Jaishree was riding the motorcycle and therefore, it will have to be inferred that she was riding the two-wheeler.
12. It is nodoubt true that both the IMV report indicates that there was no damage to both the two wheelers i.e., one driven by Paramesh and the one allegedly NC: 2024:KHC:45514 driven by Jaishree.
However, since it is the admitted case of both the parties that an accident did occur, this Mr. R. Parmesh vs Mr. Kandan.

4 IMV report cannot be of any reliance.
Even according to Kandan, the two - wheeler driven by Paramesh did suffer a skid and it should have therefore indicated some damage.
The fact that Paramesh also contends that there was a collision and he also suffered injuries, this would also indicate that there must have been a damage to the vehicle.
13. In light of the evidence of both the parties that there was an accident, there must have been a resultant damage atleast to the motor cycle driven by Paramesh.
Since the IMV report is contrary to the admitted case of the parties, reliance can be placed on said document.
14. The net result of this discussion is that the vehicle owned by Kandan was driven by his daughter who did not possess a driving licence.
In other words, the vehicle owned by Kandan was being driven in NC: 2024:KHC:45514 violation of the policy conditions.

It is settled law in the case of Yellavva1 that in the event of breach of policy conditions, the insurer would still be liable to pay the compensation, if the vehicle was covered with the policy and thereafter proceed to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
Consequently, the insurer would have to pay the compensation and thereafter proceed to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
To this extent, the finding of the Tribunal is modified.

15. However, an argument was advanced by the insurer that whenever the owner of the offending vehicle, who has committed a breach of policy condition, prefers an appeal the principle of pay and recovery cannot be applied.

This Court in the case of Yellavva's case has refuted this assertion and held that the filing of an appeal by the owner of the New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Yallavva and Another, ILR 2020 KAR 2239 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:45514 offending vehicle would have no bearing on the liability of the insurer, and the principle of 'pay and recover' would have to be applied.

sentences.text: Consequently, this argument is rejected.
16. The compensation awarded by Tribunal are just and proper except the sums awarded towards 'loss of future income' and 'loss of income during laid-up period.
17. The Tribunal has assessed the disability at 10% which is also just and proper.

It has, however,
adopted a notional income of Rs.9,500/- and since the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has fixed a sum of Rs.11,000/- for the accidents of the year 2017, it would be appropriate to adopt the said notional income.

As a consequence, the claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,98,000/-
(Rs.11,000/- x 12 x '15' x 10%) towards 'loss of future income'.

The Tribunal has taken the laid-up period as two months and since the monthly income has been taken as Rs.11,000/-, the claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.22,000/- towards 'loss of income during Mr. R. Parmesh vs Mr. Kandan.

at the time of filing the appeal and has made a further deposit of Rs.1,00,000/-.
In total, he has deposited Rs.1,25,000/-.

Since this Court has consistently awarded interest at the rate of 6% per annum, the rate of interest is also modified to 6% per annum.
Consequently, the appeals are disposed of in the above mentioned terms.

22. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:45514 from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
23.
The other aspects of the Award of the Tribunal remain undisturbed.
24. This appeal is, accordingly, allowed in part.
